sections.title: RDS Fundamentals, Storage Auto Scaling & Read Replicas
keyTopics: RDS vs self-managed DB on EC2
sections.objective: Choose RDS over EC2-hosted databases and decide when to use read replicas (async, up to 15) versus Multi-AZ (sync, one DNS name, automatic failover) for scaling, DR and cost.

sections.title: Aurora: Architecture, Endpoints, Serverless, Global & Integrations
sections.objective: Explain Aurora's HA storage design, endpoint selection, Serverless and Global Database trade-offs, and pick Aurora features (custom endpoints, ML, Babelfish) for a given workload scenario.

sections.title: Backups, Restore and Security for RDS & Aurora
keyTopics: Stopped RDS still billed for storage
sections.objective: Design backup/retention and restore strategies, apply RDS/Aurora encryption and access controls, and decide when RDS Proxy improves resilience and connection efficiency.

sections.title: ElastiCache: Redis vs Memcached, Security & Caching Patterns
sections.objective: Select Redis or Memcached based on HA, persistence and sharding needs, and apply caching patterns (lazy loading, write-through, session store) with correct security and invalidation choices.

notes: Chapter is heavily scenario-tested against Task 3.3 (read replicas, caching, engines), Task 2.2 (Multi-AZ, failover, RDS Proxy) and Task 4.3 (snapshot vs stop, Serverless for intermittent workloads). Watch the classic distractors: Multi-AZ is DR/failover, not read scaling; read replicas are async and eventually consistent, so apps must change the connection string; unencrypted master cannot have encrypted replicas; restoring a snapshot never overwrites the original. RDS Proxy reduces failover time and is never public. Exam-guide additions: storage auto scaling aligns to Task 4.1; proxy concepts are explicitly named in Task 2.2.
